protocol.py: 4 biology problems (1 warning, 3 notes).

1. WARNING WELL-CAPACITY: More liquid than the well is rated for: 300 ul against 200 ul, 3
wells
   line 45:  p300_multi.dispense(20, plate[well])
   At line 45 the robot filled wells F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3 past the 200 ul the maker
   states for it (this line did it 3 times), reaching 300 ul, under the 368 ul the well
   holds to its rim. Above the stated maximum the liquid climbs the wall and wets the seal,
   a tip going in displaces it over the edge, and the volumes still add up on paper, so the
   plate map does not see it and the simulator says nothing. Wells: wells F1, G1 and H1 in
   slot 3.
   Affected: wells F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Use labware rated for the volume, or scale every volume down so the fullest well
   stays under the stated maximum with room to mix.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [ff10ce791875]

2. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 8 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 45:  p300_multi.dispense(20, plate[well])
   At line 45 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot
   3), and 8 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the
   mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated,
   or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate
   can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 20 ul of master mix and 5 ul of water in place of
   the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [228002daa387]

3. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 2 wells never mixed after sample 3 and sample 1 went in (17 to 20%
of the well)
   line 45:  p300_multi.dispense(20, plate[well])
   At line 45 the robot added sample 3 and sample 1 to wells C1 and H1 in slot 3, which
   already held sample 1, master mix, sample 3 and sample 2 (this line did it twice). The
   addition was 17 to 20% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended
   with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what
   the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually
   vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells C1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells C1 and H1 in slot 3 after line 45: `mix_after=(5, 84 to 240)` on the
   transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 84 to 240, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the
   well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [32ca9801d5c8]

4. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 6 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 4, sample 5 and
2 more went in (2 to 20% of the well)
   line 54:  p20_single.dispense(5, plate[dst])
   At line 54 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 4, sample 5 and 2 more to wells A1,
   B1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3, which already held master mix, sample 1, sample 3 and
   sample 2 (this line did it 6 times). The addition was 2 to 20% of the well, nothing mixed
   the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small
   well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you
   calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one
   will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, B1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3 after line 54: `mix_after=(5, 20 to
   212)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20 to 212, well)`, with the volume about 80% of
   what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [25c0f88d97eb]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
